claude.country: Not reported (public US cohorts CPTAC-PDAC and TCGA-PAAD; authors' future work references Turkey)
claude.sample_unit: tumor samples (140 CPTAC discovery, 150 TCGA external)

links.outcome: Conformal coverage under zero-shot transfer versus local recalibration on target-cohort sample
links.effect: Zero-shot coverage plateaued near 0.85 at alpha=0.05; recalibrating on 37 held-out TCGA samples restored nominal coverage (split-conformal 0.984, 0.973, 0.893 at alpha 0.05, 0.10, 0.20).
links.quote: In contrast, recalibrating the conformal layer on a held-out TCGA split (Regime 3; 37 calibration samples, all of the minority class), with the classifier still trained only on CPTAC and exposed to no TCGA label during training, restored nominal coverage at every level

links.outcome: Discrimination of a CPTAC-trained classifier on an external, independent cohort versus internal cross-validation
links.effect: Internal nested CV AUROC ~0.96; external TCGA AUROC 0.913-0.938 (ensemble 0.961), with a small gap (0.959 to 0.938 for GNB) versus typical 5-15 point drops.
links.quote: First, the modest ΔAUROC of −0.021 for Gaussian Naïve Bayes between internal cross-validation and external evaluation (0.959 → 0.938) is among the smallest cross-cohort gaps reported in the PDAC subtype literature

links.outcome: Dataset shift between development and external cohorts affecting performance and conformal validity
links.effect: Minimal batch effect on discrimination (cohort AUROC 0.58; 1.0% variance to cohort) but exchangeability violation caused ~10-point conformal undercoverage (~0.85 vs 0.95 target).
links.quote: All four conformal procedures converged to a coverage ceiling of approximately 0.85 at α = 0.05, despite targeting 0.95—a residual 10-percentage-point undercoverage.

links.outcome: Whether per-patient conformal uncertainty flags borderline tumors via abstention
links.effect: Abstention was 14.0% (margin <0.25), 19.5% (0.25-0.50), 5.3% (0.50-1.00), and 0% (>1.0), concentrating on borderline tumors that warrant manual review.
links.quote: That is, the conformal predictor abstained precisely on the biologically borderline tumors—providing a principled mechanism for flagging cases that warrant manual pathology review.

links.outcome: Reliability of reference-standard subtype labels (Moffitt vs PurIST agreement)
links.effect: Moffitt-PurIST agreement 78.6% (kappa 0.54) in CPTAC and 70.7% (kappa 0.42) in TCGA; labels derived from signature raise circularity concern.
links.quote: The Moffitt and PurIST subtype labels agreed in 78.6% of CPTAC samples (Cohen’s κ = 0.54, 95% CI 0.40–0.67) and 70.7% of TCGA samples (κ = 0.42, 0.30–0.54), corresponding to moderate agreement.

links.outcome: Suitability for autonomous use versus decision-support given conformal undercoverage
links.effect: Even best procedure (CRC) reached only 85.3% coverage vs 95% target; authors do not recommend autonomous use and confine tool to decision support under expert oversight.
links.quote: However, because even CRC attains only 85.3% empirical coverage against the 0.95 target, we explicitly do not recommend any of these procedures for autonomous clinical use at α = 0.05.

links.outcome: external discrimination generalization
links.effect: Gaussian Naïve Bayes AUROC changed 0.959 → 0.938 (Δ −0.021) from internal to external validation.
links.quote: First, the modest ΔAUROC of −0.021 for Gaussian Naïve Bayes between internal cross-validation and external evaluation (0.959 → 0.938) is among the smallest cross-cohort gaps reported in the PDAC subtype literature, and contrasts favorably with the 5–15 percentage point deterioration typical in transcriptomic cancer-subtype classifiers [ 11 , 12 ].

links.outcome: reference label agreement
links.effect: Moffitt-PurIST agreement was 78.6% in CPTAC (κ=0.54) and 70.7% in TCGA (κ=0.42).
links.quote: The Moffitt and PurIST subtype labels agreed in 78.6% of CPTAC samples (Cohen’s κ = 0.54, 95% CI 0.40–0.67) and 70.7% of TCGA samples (κ = 0.42, 0.30–0.54), corresponding to moderate agreement.

links.outcome: calibration versus discrimination
links.effect: Ensemble ECE 0.067 vs Gaussian Naïve Bayes 0.031; ensemble F1 0.894 vs 0.916 despite discrimination gain.
links.quote: This discrimination gain came at a calibration cost, however: the ensemble was the least well-calibrated model (ECE = 0.067, versus 0.031 for Gaussian Naïve Bayes) and did not surpass Gaussian Naïve Bayes in F1 (0.894 versus 0.916), so the single Gaussian Naïve Bayes model remains preferable where well-calibrated probabilities are required.

links.outcome: algorithm selection comparison
links.effect: Mean AUROC ranged 0.902–0.962; only sklearn-GBM was significantly inferior by Wilcoxon (adjusted p = 0.008), not corrected t-test.
links.quote: After Holm adjustment, the corrected resampled t -test identified no algorithm as differing significantly from Extra Trees; only sklearn-GBM, the weakest performer (0.902, 0.866–0.938), was significantly inferior under the Wilcoxon test (adjusted p = 0.008), and not under the corrected t -test (adjusted p = 0.15).

links.outcome: cross-cohort exchangeability failure
links.effect: Zero-shot conformal coverage plateaued near 0.85 at α=0.05 versus 0.95 target, attributed to cross-cohort non-exchangeability.
links.quote: This recovery demonstrates that the zero-shot failure is a property of cross-cohort non-exchangeability and not of the conformal machinery.

links.outcome: target-cohort recalibration coverage
links.effect: Target-cohort recalibration with 37 TCGA calibration samples restored split-conformal coverage: 0.984±0.016, 0.973±0.022, 0.893±0.045.
links.quote: In contrast, recalibrating the conformal layer on a held-out TCGA split (Regime 3; 37 calibration samples, all of the minority class), with the classifier still trained only on CPTAC and exposed to no TCGA label during training, restored nominal coverage at every level (split-conformal 0.984 ± 0.016, 0.973 ± 0.022 and 0.893 ± 0.045 at α = 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20, respectively, each meeting or exceeding its 1 − α target; mean ± SD over 20 random calibration/test splits).

links.outcome: abstention for uncertain tumors
links.effect: Abstention was 14.0%, 19.5%, 5.3%, and 0% across increasing Moffitt margin strata.
links.quote: Importantly, abstention behaved as theoretically expected with respect to the Moffitt label-assignment margin ( Supplementary Figure S2 ): samples with a margin below 0.25 had a 14.0% abstention rate, samples with a margin of 0.25–0.50 had a 19.5% rate, samples with a margin of 0.50–1.00 had a 5.3% rate, and samples with a margin above 1.0 had a 0% rate.

links.outcome: uncertainty coverage
links.effect: At α=0.05, CRC coverage 0.853; split 0.847; weighted 0.847; CV+ 0.780, below 0.95 nominal.
links.quote: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) achieved the highest empirical coverage at α = 0.05 (0.853; abstention rate 0.0%; mean set size 1.000), followed by unweighted Mondrian split-conformal (0.847), weighted Mondrian (0.847), and CV+ (0.780).

links.outcome: Conformal coverage across significance levels after local target-cohort recalibration

links.quote: In contrast, recalibrating the conformal layer on a held-out TCGA split (Regime 3; 37 calibration samples, all of the minority class), with the classifier still trained only on CPTAC and exposed to no TCGA label during training, restored nominal coverage at every level (split-conformal 0.984 ± 0.016, 0.973 ± 0.022 and 0.893 ± 0.045 at α = 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20, respectively, each meeting or exceeding its 1 − α target; mean ± SD over 20 random calibration/test splits).

links.outcome: Abstention rate across tumor label-assignment margin strata
links.effect: Abstention was 14.0% for margin <0.25, 19.5% for 0.25-0.50, 5.3% for 0.50-1.00, and 0% for margin >1.0.
links.quote: Importantly, abstention behaved as theoretically expected with respect to the Moffitt label-assignment margin (Supplementary Figure S2): samples with a margin below 0.25 had a 14.0% abstention rate, samples with a margin of 0.25–0.50 had a 19.5% rate, samples with a margin of 0.50–1.00 had a 5.3% rate, and samples with a margin above 1.0 had a 0% rate.

screen.practice: local recalibration and conformal uncertainty quantification
screen.reason: The study develops and externally validates a molecular subtype classifier for PDAC while specifically evaluating conformal prediction methods and demonstrating that local recalibration on target samples restores coverage under domain shift.
